definition: To officially become operative, legally valid, and binding as a law or regulation.
example: The strict automotive emissions regulations will come into force at the start of the next fiscal year.
commonMistake: ❌ enter into power / walk to legal force → ✔ come into force / take effect

definition: To perform an unlawful, criminal deed in violation of the legal code.
example: Youths who commit a minor crime should be directed towards restorative community service.
commonMistake: ❌ make a crime / do a crime → ✔ commit a crime / perpetrate an offence
ieltsTip: Never say 'do a crime' or 'make a crime'.

definition: To officially and formally announce the commencement of armed hostilities against an enemy.
example: Under constitutional law, parliament retains the sole sovereign authority to declare war.
commonMistake: ❌ speak war out / announce battle fight → ✔ declare war

definition: The trail of recorded data and browsing history left by an individual when using the internet.
example: Secondary pupils should be instructed on maintaining a prudent and professional digital footprint.
commonMistake: ❌ internet shoe trace / cyber mark → ✔ a digital footprint

definition: To permanently quit secondary or tertiary education prior to graduation.
example: Targeted vocational apprenticeships significantly reduce the percentage of adolescents who drop out of school.
commonMistake: ❌ fall out from school / abandon study mid-way → ✔ drop out of school

definition: To officially formulate precise, unambiguous rules or standards to regulate conduct.
example: Regulatory agencies must establish clear guidelines regarding the commercial application of gene editing.
commonMistake: ❌ make clean rules / put bright guidelines → ✔ establish clear guidelines / set forth protocols

definition: The main, prominent title of the most important article on the first page of a newspaper.
example: The corporate tax investigation remained the lead front-page headline for three consecutive days.
commonMistake: ❌ first-paper title / head-line on front cover → ✔ a front-page headline / banner headline
ieltsTip: Media influence and news culture essays.

definition: Deep, serious, and acute anxiety regarding an alarming public danger or crisis.
example: The unchecked proliferation of algorithmic synthetic deepfakes is a matter of grave concern.
commonMistake: ❌ heavy deep worry / tomb-dark concern → ✔ grave concern / deep concern

definition: Severe, strict, and rigorous disciplinary consequences imposed on offenders.
example: Criminologists debate whether harsh punishment serves as an effective deterrent against recidivism.
commonMistake: ❌ heavy pain penalty / cruel-stiff sanction → ✔ harsh punishment / severe sanctions

definition: A very large, substantial, and punitive financial penalty.
example: Corporations caught dumping untreated wastewater face a hefty fine from environmental regulators.
commonMistake: ❌ heavy-weight fine / big money punishment → ✔ a hefty fine / a substantial penalty

definition: The level of wealth, comfort, material goods, and necessities available to a socio-economic class.
example: Industrialisation drastically improved general living standards while exacerbating environmental pollution.
commonMistake: ❌ life quality ranks / everyday staying level → ✔ living standards / standard of living

definition: An issue of utmost, existential urgency upon which human survival directly depends.
example: Securing prompt humanitarian water shipments was literally a matter of life and death for drought victims.
commonMistake: ❌ question of dead or living / life-kill problem → ✔ a matter of life and death

definition: The reporting of an issue, person, or event in newspapers, on television, or online.
example: Excessive sensationalist media coverage often skews public perceptions of violent crime rates.
commonMistake: ❌ press reporting-volume / media blanket-show → ✔ media coverage / press coverage
ieltsTip: Media literacy and public opinion prompts.

definition: To formally vote for and adopt a legislative measure into national code.
example: The legislature passed a landmark law guaranteeing paid paternity leave for public servants.
commonMistake: ❌ walk a law through / make a law go → ✔ pass a law / approve a statute

definition: To formally state in a court of law that one is responsible for a crime.
example: The corporate accountant chose to plead guilty in exchange for a reduced custodial sentence.
commonMistake: ❌ say guilty / admit guilt-word → ✔ plead guilty

definition: An intense expression of widespread anger, disapproval, and protest by the populace.
example: The proposal to privatize regional water services provoked a furious public outcry.
commonMistake: ❌ people shouting anger / broad screaming out → ✔ a public outcry / popular backlash

definition: To bring back an order of harmony, calmness, and cessation of armed violence.
example: Multinational peacekeeping forces were mandated to restore peace in the fractured border territory.
commonMistake: ❌ rebuild calm / bring back friendly silence → ✔ restore peace

definition: To remain in a prison facility for the full period ordered by a judicial court.
example: Inmates who serve a lengthy custodial sentence frequently struggle to reintegrate into civil society.
commonMistake: ❌ stay a prison time / sit a jail order → ✔ serve a sentence

definition: To legally ratify and enter into a formal contract ending war between sovereign states.
example: Warring factions agreed to sign a historic peace treaty mediated by the international court.
commonMistake: ❌ write name on peace paper / make peace agreement → ✔ sign a peace treaty / ratify a peace accord

definition: Living quarters providing ample physical room, breadth, and comfort.
example: Suburban families often trade compact inner-city flats for spacious accommodation with gardens.
commonMistake: ❌ wide-room house / large space dwelling → ✔ spacious accommodation

definition: Fair, generous, and polite behavior or treatment of others, especially in a sports contest.
example: Schools should instill a spirit of sportsmanship rather than an obsessive win-at-all-costs mindset.
commonMistake: ❌ sports manner / fair-play kindness → ✔ sportsmanship / sense of fair play

definition: To appear before a judicial court to be judged on criminal charges.
example: The former corporate treasurer was formally ordered to stand trial for insider trading.
commonMistake: ❌ face court judge / be in test room → ✔ stand trial

definition: A temporary period of governmental crisis governance declared due to natural disasters or civil strife.
example: The prime minister declared an official state of emergency after unprecedented flash floods engulfed the province.
commonMistake: ❌ emergency situation decree / danger status → ✔ a state of emergency

definition: A popular destination that attracts large multitudes of international holidaymakers.
example: Local civic authorities in the tourist hotspot introduced caps on cruise ship dockings.
commonMistake: ❌ tourist hot place / popular travel dot → ✔ a tourist hotspot / a tourist magnet

definition: A state of overcrowded roads where vehicular movement is significantly slowed or stopped.
example: Implementing congestion charges helps alleviate chronic traffic congestion in inner city cores.
commonMistake: ❌ car jamming / auto block-up → ✔ traffic congestion / vehicular gridlock

definition: Lively, exciting, and varied evening leisure and entertainment activities in a town.
example: University towns often attract prospective applicants due to their vibrant nightlife and arts scene.
commonMistake: ❌ alive night entertainment / active dark-time fun → ✔ vibrant nightlife

definition: To gradually collect, amass, and build up financial assets over an extended period.
example: Financial advisors emphasize that disciplined index investing allows households to accumulate wealth over decades.
commonMistake: ❌ gather riches / pile up cash-fortune → ✔ accumulate wealth / amass capital

definition: A film that achieves massive financial success and high ticket sales in cinemas.
example: The superhero franchise established itself as the summer's biggest international box-office hit.
commonMistake: ❌ cinema ticket win / theatre money-maker → ✔ a box-office hit / a commercial blockbuster

definition: To make steady professional progress toward senior executive positions.
example: Graduates are often willing to work unpaid overtime to climb the career ladder faster.
commonMistake: ❌ go up the job steps / elevate career stairs → ✔ climb the career ladder
ieltsTip: Idiomatic yet standard for career and employment Task 2 essays.

definition: To generate sufficient income to cover fundamental sustenance and living costs.
example: Street vendors labor long hours under extreme climate conditions merely to earn a decent living.
commonMistake: ❌ win life money / get a living → ✔ earn a living / make a living

definition: Extremely intense, aggressive rivalry between organizations.
example: Budget carriers engage in fierce competition over short-haul European leisure corridors.
commonMistake: ❌ wild fight / hot market competition → ✔ fierce competition / intense rivalry
ieltsTip: Examiner favorite for business and market economics essays.

definition: To become legally declared unable to repay outstanding debts.
example: Several high-street retail chains went bankrupt during the prolonged macroeconomic slump.
commonMistake: ❌ become bankrupt / turn to bankruptcy → ✔ go bankrupt / enter liquidation

definition: To formally notify an employer of one's intention to resign from a position.
example: Dissatisfied with stagnant remuneration, the lead software engineer decided to hand in her notice.
commonMistake: ❌ give one's leaving letter / pass resignation note → ✔ hand in one's notice / tender one's resignation
ieltsTip: Speaking Part 2 narrative and workplace essays.

definition: An excessively large amount of professional duties assigned to an employee.
example: Junior medical personnel routinely suffer acute burnout due to an unmanageable and heavy workload.
commonMistake: ❌ big work volume / weighty task burden → ✔ a heavy workload

definition: The degree of fulfillment, happiness, and contentment an employee derives from their occupation.
example: Recent surveys indicate that autonomy and mentorship contribute more to job satisfaction than base salary.
commonMistake: ❌ work happiness / career pleasure → ✔ job satisfaction

definition: To introduce, release, or make a new commercial good available to consumers for the first time.
example: Tech conglomerates invest millions in synchronized marketing campaigns prior to launching a product.
commonMistake: ❌ shoot out a product / push a merchandise alive → ✔ launch a product / introduce a product

definition: To spend more money than one earns, leading to debt and instability.
example: Easy access to unsecured credit lines encourages impressionable consumers to live beyond their means.
commonMistake: ❌ spend over one's wallet / live outside earnings → ✔ live beyond one's means

definition: To earn more money through commercial sales than the total expenses incurred.
example: It often takes up to three operating quarters for tech startups to make a profit.
commonMistake: ❌ earn profit / gain profit (in informal contexts) → ✔ make a profit / turn a profit

definition: The portion or percentage of an industry's sales that is controlled by a particular firm.
example: Innovative electric vehicle manufacturers have captured a rapidly growing market share.
commonMistake: ❌ trade piece / market percentage slice → ✔ market share

definition: The lowest hourly remuneration that employers may legally pay their workers.
example: Raising the national statutory minimum wage helps alleviate in-work poverty for low-skilled laborers.
commonMistake: ❌ bottom salary / smallest legal pay → ✔ the minimum wage

definition: To enjoy the beneficial consequences, returns, or fruits of one's earlier efforts.
example: Societies that invest in universal nursery education eventually reap the economic rewards decades later.
commonMistake: ❌ harvest the gifts / pick the winning fruits → ✔ reap the rewards / reap the benefits
alternativePartners: enjoy the fruits of one's labor

definition: To manage, direct, and oversee the daily operations of a commercial enterprise.
example: Young entrepreneurs face significant regulatory burdens when attempting to run a business in developing markets.
commonMistake: ❌ make a business / do a business → ✔ run a business / operate an enterprise
ieltsTip: Fundamental collocation: never say 'do a business'.

definition: To postpone, cancel, or suspend consideration of a proposal indefinitely.
example: Facing ferocious local resistance, the municipal developer decided to shelve the controversial highway plan.
commonMistake: ❌ put plan on bookshelf / delay a plan away → ✔ shelve a plan / postpone an initiative

definition: A financial spending plan that allows very little leeway for discretionary or unnecessary expense.
example: Students living on a tight budget must plan grocery expenditures with meticulous care.
commonMistake: ❌ narrow money-plan / strict wallet limit → ✔ a tight budget
ieltsTip: Personal finance and public spending essays.
